messages:
julia: quick sync: proposing a 'token slimming' pattern to shrink long-lived API key surface. idea: only a tiny set of long-lived admin keys, mint short-lived intent tokens for most flows. want quick takes before RFC.

mike: +1. main questions: runtime-derived claims (no mint) vs ephemeral minted tokens. latency/cache tradeoffs.

sarah: runtime derivation helps avoid mint load but needs a low-latency claim cache and clear TTL rules. short TTLs reduce risk but increase mint frequency.

cory: minted tokens give revocation and clean audit trails, but add a mint infra surface (rate limits, auth, retries). ops will need throttles.

julia: thinking hybrid: router attempts to mint for sensitive write paths; low-risk read routes use deterministic claim expansion (cached). minted tokens include explicit intent claims so policy engine sees the same attributes.

alexa: must preserve lineage for billing/audit. include original principal as a `parent` claim in minted tokens or emit `X-Orig-Actor` at mint time. do not log secrets.

mike: agree on lineage; watch metric cardinality. use stable labels (org, project, principal-type) not token ids.

sarah: RBAC mapping: translate claims to existing role ids via static policy mappings. avoid dynamic per-token roles to keep audits simple.

cory: external customer keys (embedded in apps) — can't force immediate ephemeral-only. plan: accept legacy keys during migration, shadow-mint tokens and emit deprecation telemetry, then progressively throttle.

julia: migration plan: 1) shadow-mint and log lineage; 2) deprecation warnings in dashboard/responses; 3) provide SDK auto-mint helpers. router accepts both during rollout.

alexa: example mapping snippet (pseudo):
```
match: project:proj-123:key:ABCD
mint_to: {sub: "svc:edge", aud: "inference", claims: ["read:dataset:proj-123"], exp: now + 900, parent: "user:alice@acme"}
```

mike: ensure SSO/audit pipelines capture `parent`. otherwise we lose trigger attribution.

sarah: enforcement: policy engine evaluates only `claims` and `aud`. `parent` is audit-only. document that in RFC.

cory: ops notes: mint service must be highly available and per-customer throttled. failure modes: if mint fails, fallback to cached deterministic claim for a brief grace period, then deny. document circuit-breaker.

julia: fallback chain: minted token -> cached derived claim -> deny. set SLOs for mint service and plan a canary rollout.

deploy-bot: started canary rollout for token-slimmer experiment (eng-sre) https://deploys.internal/redwood/rollouts/3333

alexa: i'll draft RFC sections: token shapes, claim vocab, migration timeline, metrics (shadow-mint rate, lineage-loss rate, label cardinality), ops SLOs. need owners.

julia: owners: julia (RFC lead), mike + sarah (policy/telemetry reviewers), cory (mint-service reliability), alexa (migration SDK/docs). target RFC in two weeks (2026-04-04).

mike: i'll add instrumentation notes to limit cardinality.

sarah: i'll prepare policy examples and mapping table.

cory: i'll diagram failure modes and default throttles.

julia: thanks all — i'll open the RFC draft tomorrow and ping reviewers. :rocket:
